entries.providerBehavior: GitHub PR review state is split across merged/state/draft flags and the native reviewDecision, which may disagree with the raw state.
entries.expectedNormalizedOutcome: Every PR variant maps to one closed DeliveryRequestReviewState; a merged or closed PR never reports open; an unrecognized native reviewDecision resolves to the declared open fallback instead of a silent default, and a flattening regression fails by trap name.

entries.providerBehavior: A commit can carry several check runs per SHA plus a check-suite roll-up whose conclusion can be greener than an individual run.
entries.expectedNormalizedOutcome: read-pipeline-run for the SHA returns every check run as a job with a closed-set state and trace evidence where a details URL exists; a failed run is never hidden behind the roll-up and SHAs yield disjoint sets.

entries.providerBehavior: GitHub issue payloads carry labels, an optional assignee, open/closed state, an optional updated_at, issue links, and a state_reason on live closed issues.
entries.expectedNormalizedOutcome: Issues normalize to WorkItem with labels, an optional assignee, a closed-set status alias (open to ready, closed to done), updatedAt verbatim when present (absent otherwise), and typed relations only when the payload records them. state_reason is not modeled: closed maps to done regardless of not_planned, and live-shape revalidation plus any canceled distinction is deferred to M0-S20. labelled `review`/`in-progress` issues resolve to `in-review`/`in-progress` by declared precedence, and an exact-case label equal to a declared `label-swap` token wins

entries.providerBehavior: The repository issue-list endpoint returns both issues and pull-request objects in one page.
entries.expectedNormalizedOutcome: listWorkItems skips every object carrying a pull_request property before normalization, so the returned WorkItem set contains no pull-request object while the raw page size is preserved for the source-at-limit signal.

entries.providerBehavior: List reads are unbounded unless the client sends one declared per_page limit, and the raw returned page size can equal that limit.
entries.expectedNormalizedOutcome: Each list read sends exactly one page with state=open, the declared per_page limit, and the declared updated-descending sort; the raw page size is reported separately from the filtered item count so a full page signals possible truncation.

entries.providerBehavior: The real GitHub REST issue list does not supply structured issue dependency links.
entries.expectedNormalizedOutcome: An issue without issue_links normalizes to relations: [], and the tracker source declares blocked-dependency relations unavailable rather than empty.

entries.providerBehavior: The GitHub pull-request list payload carries state/draft/head/base but no review decision or review threads.
entries.expectedNormalizedOutcome: The list read normalizes refs/draft/state and leaves the absent review decision and threads untrusted, so status reports those item signals unknown instead of open or zero.

entries.providerBehavior: A work item can have several closed PRs; only merged PRs whose source ref follows the branch convention are candidates, and the merged head is copied verbatim or stays absent.
entries.expectedNormalizedOutcome: Lookup selects the highest numeric matching merged entity deterministically and copies head.sha; an absent head never fabricates a value.

entries.providerBehavior: GitHub label updates are a full-array replace, so a named remove/add must preserve every unnamed label.
entries.expectedNormalizedOutcome: write-work-item removes only named lifecycle labels, adds delivered, and preserves change and vendor labels.

entries.providerBehavior: Review-thread resolution is a GraphQL mutation behind the existing injected transport, not a REST write.
entries.expectedNormalizedOutcome: resolve-delivery-thread posts one GraphQL mutation with the thread id and succeeds on a resolved thread payload.

entries.providerBehavior: Null mergeability means unknown, never mergeable.
entries.expectedNormalizedOutcome: Null mergeability means unknown, never mergeable.

entries.providerBehavior: A false/dirty mergeability is conflicting.
entries.expectedNormalizedOutcome: A false/dirty mergeability is conflicting.

entries.providerBehavior: A blocked state is not-mergeable even when mergeable is true.
entries.expectedNormalizedOutcome: A blocked state is not-mergeable even when mergeable is true.

entries.providerBehavior: An absent head SHA stays absent.
entries.expectedNormalizedOutcome: An absent head SHA stays absent.

entries.providerBehavior: Absent commits/changed_files stay absent.
entries.expectedNormalizedOutcome: Absent commits/changed_files stay absent.

entries.providerBehavior: Zero commits is not a non-vacuous surface.
entries.expectedNormalizedOutcome: Zero commits is not a non-vacuous surface.

entries.providerBehavior: Zero check runs is not green.
entries.expectedNormalizedOutcome: Zero check runs is not green.

entries.providerBehavior: All-skipped check runs are not green.
entries.expectedNormalizedOutcome: All-skipped check runs are not green.

entries.providerBehavior: A page at 100 runs is truncated.
entries.expectedNormalizedOutcome: A page at 100 runs is truncated.

entries.providerBehavior: An issue without comments exposes labels only.
entries.expectedNormalizedOutcome: An issue without comments exposes labels only.

entries.providerBehavior: A PR-list HTTP 404 is definitive absence.
entries.expectedNormalizedOutcome: A PR-list HTTP 404 is definitive absence.

entries.providerBehavior: A matched PR-detail HTTP 404 is head-unresolved for detail-consuming gates.
entries.expectedNormalizedOutcome: A matched PR-detail HTTP 404 is head-unresolved for detail-consuming gates.

entries.providerBehavior: A check-run HTTP 404 is unknown read-failed with source absent.
entries.expectedNormalizedOutcome: A check-run HTTP 404 is unknown read-failed with source absent.

entries.providerBehavior: A work-item HTTP 404 is ticket-unresolved with source absent.
entries.expectedNormalizedOutcome: A work-item HTTP 404 is ticket-unresolved with source absent.

entries.providerBehavior: Non-2xx GitHub read responses fold into the adapter-local failure types whose only discriminant used to be the prose detail string.
entries.expectedNormalizedOutcome: The read slice carries the structured numeric httpStatus on every non-2xx response and omits it on transport failures; the field is secret-free, the adapter-local identity is unchanged, and no prose is copied into it.

entries.providerBehavior: A squash landing accepts a crafted commit title and message and echoes the landed commit identity.
entries.expectedNormalizedOutcome: Both crafted strings are transmitted byte-identically, merge_method is squash, and the outcome carries the provider-supplied merge commit identity.

entries.providerBehavior: A successful landing response omits the landing commit identity.
entries.expectedNormalizedOutcome: The outcome stays merged with no mergeCommitSha member: absence is unknown and is never derived from a branch head or a local commit.

entries.providerBehavior: The expected head no longer matches the pull request head.
entries.expectedNormalizedOutcome: The guard is transmitted verbatim and the mismatch is one classified provider.payload.invalid refusal with the structured status, one request, and no retry.

entries.providerBehavior: The provider refuses with an already-merged refusal; merged truth is asserted only by a read-back.
entries.expectedNormalizedOutcome: Success is returned only when the read-back observes merged true; an unmerged read-back leaves the classified refusal standing, and the landing is never retried.

entries.providerBehavior: `gh api --include` output can carry a proxy status block before the authoritative one.
entries.expectedNormalizedOutcome: The final status block decides the status and the remaining bytes are the body; an unparsable or absent status block is refused instead of being assumed to be 200.

entries.providerBehavior: An already-shaped request arrives with an Authorization header the CLI must not forward.
entries.expectedNormalizedOutcome: The credential appears only as GH_TOKEN in the constructed child environment; argv carries no credential, the header is removed from the forwarded headers, and the isolated GH_CONFIG_DIR plus prompt suppression are present.

entries.providerBehavior: A carrier-free human comment write reaches the issue comment surface with no metadata envelope and no declared carrier.
entries.expectedNormalizedOutcome: The recorded request body is exactly the human text, no envelope block or carrier marker is present, the declaration keeps empty carrier arrays, and the provider comment identity is returned.

entries.providerBehavior: A delivery-request create/update is a content write; the provider also exposes a landing surface that must never be used by it.
entries.expectedNormalizedOutcome: A create posts the head/base refs, title and body verbatim and returns the normalized delivery-request view; no landing request and no merge-state write occurs, and an update never creates.

entries.providerBehavior: GitHub issues carry either a native state or lifecycle labels, and the declared map has a load-bearing precedence order.
entries.expectedNormalizedOutcome: The four-row seed is declared in precedence order; a closed issue resolves done regardless of labels, an exact-case label wins by declared precedence, a case collision with a declared label-swap token is a visible refusal, and an unknown or absent label resolves through the native-state row.

entries.providerBehavior: GitHub check runs expose provider-native started_at and completed_at timestamps that may be absent or partial.
entries.expectedNormalizedOutcome: PipelineJob.startedAt and completedAt copy the provider strings verbatim when present; an absent timestamp stays absent, an incomplete run has no completion time, and no duration or default is ever derived.

entries.providerBehavior: GitHub job log text can exceed the fixed excerpt cap and can contain multi-byte characters anywhere, including across the byte boundary.
entries.expectedNormalizedOutcome: The excerpt is a faithful UTF-8 byte prefix of at most 8192 bytes that never splits a multi-byte sequence, byteLength equals the returned bytes, and truncated is the sole truncation authority.

entries.providerBehavior: A review thread can carry more comments than the cap and individual comment bodies can exceed the per-body byte cap, including multi-byte text across the boundary.
entries.expectedNormalizedOutcome: At most 50 oldest-first provider-ordered comments are returned with the provider total preserved, each body is a UTF-8 byte prefix of at most 4096 bytes that never splits a multi-byte sequence, and the thread-level truncated flag is true exactly when comments were dropped or a body was truncated.
